verdict.rationale: Datalab's own Pipelines feature stores automations as "reusable, versioned configurations." Published agent processors can be pinned to a specific version (<id>@<version>), which suggests a way to run an earlier version. The docs do not describe a review flow or an explicit rollback or restore action, and the API Version Policies page covers Datalab's own API stability rather than user automations, so it is not credited. Missing for 10: a documented review/diff workflow for pipeline changes, an explicit rollback/restore mechanism, detail on version history management, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Pipelines chain processors (convert, extract, segment, custom) into reusable, versioned configurations.
Chain processors into versioned, reusable configurations and deploy to production
Address it with processor=<id>, optionally pinned to a version as <id>@<version>
